finding.claim: typeof value is never null so `t === null` is dead code; null falls through to `value.buffer` access which throws TypeError instead of returning true as JSON-serializable.
finding.title: isJSONSerializable mishandles null and throws on value.buffer

verifier.reason: Confirmed at utils.ts:22 and utils.ts:31: typeof null is "object" so the string t can never equal null, null then passes the object check and Array.isArray check before value.buffer throws a TypeError.

finding.claim: On retry the previous timeout-derived signal which is already aborted is spread into the next $fetchRaw and combined via AbortSignal.any, so the retried request starts already aborted and fails immediately.
finding.title: Timeout retry reuses already-aborted AbortSignal

verifier.reason: The timeout handling at fetch.ts:171-178 mutates context.options.signal into an AbortSignal.timeout/AbortSignal.any result, and the retry at fetch.ts:72-75 spreads that same context.options into the next $fetchRaw, so the next pass combines a fresh timeout with the already-aborted prior signal via AbortSignal.any and the retried fetch starts aborted.

finding.claim: Any input sharing a raw string prefix with the base is returned unchanged without checking a path-segment boundary, so base /api incorrectly matches /api-v2 and skips joining.
finding.title: withBase uses raw startsWith without segment boundary

verifier.reason: The code at utils.url.ts:46-48 returns input unchanged on input.startsWith(_base) with no segment-boundary check, so withBase('/api-v2','/api') incorrectly skips joinURL at utils.url.ts:50.

finding.claim: When the URL already contains a query string, array values are appended without first deleting the existing key while scalar values use set (replace), so old values are retained and duplicated.
finding.title: withQuery appends array values without clearing existing key

verifier.reason: At utils.url.ts:86 searchParams is initialized from the existing query string, and at utils.url.ts:92-95 the array branch uses append without a preceding delete while utils.url.ts:97 uses set for scalars, so pre-existing values for that key are retained alongside the new array values.
